candidate.title: miCLIP-m6A
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina schematic, captioned A schematic overview of miCLIP-m6A: one antibody/UV/immunoprecipitation route from already sheared cellular RNA to truncated cDNA. The left Methylated RNA icon and assay-name caption identify the analyte; no material arrow connects that icon to the input as a separate shearing operation. The paired fragments are examples within this route, not independently labeled branches. iCLIP is an embedded library-preparation component. RNA isolation, library completion and sequencing are outside the drawn endpoints.

states.label: Sheared cellular RNA
features: RNA is already fragmented at the first arrow-connected workflow boundary.
Purple fragments bear red methylation marks, identified by the left Methylated RNA icon and the miCLIP-m6A scope. The two fragments illustrate a population within one route.
The depicted input is cellular RNA; the primary method includes total-RNA and poly(A)+-RNA implementations, so this boundary is not restricted to mRNA.

operations.label: Reverse-transcription truncated at binding sites
operations.description: Copy the recovered RNA into cDNA that terminates near the marked antibody-contact sites; the rightward arrow leads to the standalone blue cDNA products. This captioned interval compresses the preparation of the template: the primary method releases RNA using proteinase K before reverse transcription, leaving RNA-bound peptide remnants. The retained full-sized antibody icons mark the affected sites; their mechanistic interpretation is recorded in c_rt.
operations.mechanism: Residual RNA-linked antibody peptides impede reverse transcription and produce cDNA truncations. The primary paper also describes incorporation errors, but the assigned drawing specifically depicts truncation and contains no separate mutation-readout branch.
operations.information_effect: Transfers RNA sequence identity and the crosslink-associated termination boundary into DNA. Sequencing and alignment of a library made from these cDNAs can localize putative methylated RNA residues at single-nucleotide resolution when the antibody-specific signature is characterized. The drawn contact-to-endpoint relationship does not by itself specify an exact nucleotide offset or identify every endpoint as m6A; signatures depend on antibody, and m6Am can also be recognized.

method_scopes.rationale: All four local operations apply to the antibody-based m6A miCLIP target identified by the card title, matching collection-page heading and schematic caption. The paper’s name m6A individual-nucleotide resolution crosslinking and immunoprecipitation (miCLIP) denotes this target. Its truncation readout is depicted here without assigning a particular antibody implementation. The similarly named Hussain methylation iCLIP is explicitly distinguished by the card and is not a second depicted workflow. The primary paper supports the route and resolves two schematic simplifications as recorded in corrections.
